02 / LITERATURE

Review papers & articles

Lecture notes and research articles that provide useful introductions to relativistic hydrodynamics, gravitational theory, and related developments in theoretical physics.

RELATIVISTIC HYDRODYNAMICS

Lectures on Relativistic Hydrodynamics

Pavel Kovtun's lecture notes on relativistic fluid dynamics, covering conservation laws, hydrodynamic constitutive relations, and the theoretical foundations of fluid behaviour near equilibrium.

Read on arXiv ↗

GENERAL RELATIVITY

Lecture Notes on General Relativity

Sean Carroll's lecture notes introducing the geometric formulation of gravity, spacetime curvature, tensor calculus, and Einstein's field equations.

Read on arXiv ↗

FOUNDATIONS & CONCEPTS

Review article on Carroll physics

A related resource for exploring Carrollian physics and its connections to spacetime symmetries and non-Lorentzian limits. Consult the paper for its precise scope and applications.

Read on arXiv ↗

03 / BOOKSHELF

Books & monographs

Books are valuable for developing a systematic understanding of the mathematical framework and physical principles underlying relativistic fluid dynamics and high-energy physics.

01 / FLUID DYNAMICS

Relativistic Fluid Dynamics In and Out of Equilibrium

Paolo Romatschke and Ulrike Romatschke. Cambridge University Press, 2019.

A detailed treatment of relativistic hydrodynamics, including dissipative effects and the behaviour of fluids away from equilibrium.

Hydrodynamics Dissipation
02 / THERMAL FIELD THEORY

Thermal Field Theory

Michel Le Bellac. Cambridge University Press, 1996.

An introduction to quantum field theory at finite temperature, including thermal Green's functions and the properties of quantum systems in equilibrium.

Quantum fields Finite temperature
03 / GENERAL RELATIVITY

General Relativity

Sean Carroll's lecture notes provide a freely accessible complementary resource for studying spacetime geometry, tensors, and gravitational theory.

Access lecture notes ↗
Geometry Tensor calculus

Additional books on fluid mechanics and astrophysical applications will be added as the collection develops.

04 / LEARNING

Courses & lectures

Online courses and recorded lectures offer complementary ways to strengthen mathematical foundations and explore topics beyond the scope of a single textbook.

OPEN COURSEWARE

MIT OpenCourseWare

A collection of freely accessible university course materials. Useful for reviewing fluid mechanics, differential equations, classical mechanics, and related mathematical methods.

VIDEO LECTURES

Recorded lectures on theoretical physics

Video lectures can be useful for revisiting difficult derivations and exploring subjects such as quantum field theory, general relativity, hydrodynamics, and mathematical physics.

05 / RESEARCH TOOLS

Useful websites

These platforms are useful for discovering research papers, following developments in theoretical physics, and tracing connections between related publications.

01 / PREPRINTS

arXiv

An open-access repository of scientific preprints. Particularly useful for following developments in high-energy physics, nuclear theory, mathematical physics, and general relativity.

Preprints Open access
02 / LITERATURE DATABASE

INSPIRE-HEP

A literature and bibliographic database for high-energy physics. Useful for finding publications, authors, citation records, and related research in particle physics and theoretical high-energy physics.

Bibliography High-energy physics

06 / NOTES

Using this collection

This is a working collection rather than an exhaustive bibliography. The resources are selected for their relevance to my interests in relativistic hydrodynamics, thermal field theory, and theoretical high-energy physics.

I intend to expand the list with more specialised review articles, research papers, lecture notes, and computational resources as I encounter useful material.

Suggestions for additional resources and relevant references are welcome.
